Warehousing

Capacité d’Entrepôt

The maximum volume or quantity of goods that can be physically stored in a warehouse facility, as measured by cubic meters, pallet positions, or SKUs, and documented in warehousing contracts or inventory management systems.

Quick answer: The maximum volume or quantity of goods that can be physically stored in a warehouse facility, as measured by cubic meters, pallet positions, or SKUs, and documented in warehousing contracts or inventory management systems.

Why it matters

Capacité d’Entrepôt matters because it supports clear communication in Warehousing contexts for Freight Forwarders, Supply Chain Managers, and Customs Brokers. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as FIATA Diploma, CILT Certification, and IATA DGR.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Capacité d’Entrepôt?

In this glossary, Capacité d’Entrepôt refers to: The maximum volume or quantity of goods that can be physically stored in a warehouse facility, as measured by cubic meters, pallet positions, or SKUs, and documented in warehousing contracts or inventory management systems.

How is Capacité d’Entrepôt used in logistics?

In logistics communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "La capacité d’entrepôt doit être vérifiée dans le système de gestion des stocks avant d’accepter une nouvelle expédition afin d’éviter une surcharge."

Why does Capacité d’Entrepôt matter in logistics?

Capacité d’Entrepôt matters because it supports clear communication in Warehousing contexts for Freight Forwarders, Supply Chain Managers, and Customs Brokers. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as FIATA Diploma, CILT Certification, and IATA DGR.

Who uses Capacité d’Entrepôt?

Capacité d’Entrepôt is mainly used by Freight Forwarders, Supply Chain Managers, and Customs Brokers.

What category does Capacité d’Entrepôt belong to?

In this glossary, Capacité d’Entrepôt is grouped under Warehousing. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from Incoterms 2020 (ICC), FIATA, IATA DGR, WCO and published by Protermify Logistics as a static logistics reference page.

Definition

The maximum volume or quantity of goods that can be physically stored in a warehouse facility, as measured by cubic meters, pallet positions, or SKUs, and documented in warehousing contracts or inventory management systems.

Operational example

The warehouse capacity must be verified in the inventory management system before accepting a new shipment to avoid overstocking.

Localized term

Capacité d’Entrepôt

Localized example

La capacité d’entrepôt doit être vérifiée dans le système de gestion des stocks avant d’accepter une nouvelle expédition afin d’éviter une surcharge.
